findings: The 2026-11-07 capture of the exact canonical URL is an index only: title and ACH subscription description (lines 5-7), then a statement that the article has multiple variants and two variant URLs (lines 9-14). It contains no integration steps, prerequisites, API parameters, limits, state transitions, testing data or payment outcome claims.

The 2026-05-13 matched capture includes both web Elements/advanced and web Stripe-hosted sections in one 1017-line document (old lines 18-20 and 500-504). The new index points to these same two variant categories (new lines 13-14). The content reduction is a rendering/navigation change in the captured URL, not evidence that the old behavior was deprecated or changed.

The current source is explicitly dated 2026-05-13 in frontmatter (lines 1-8) and cites only the old raw (lines 95-97). Its Elements creation, 10-day microdeposit window, default-payment-method webhook, trial SetupIntent, and Checkout delayed-notification points are supported by old lines 42-102, 221-249, 271-300, 399-470 and 732-769; they cannot be confirmed as current by the index.

Old web Elements section advises new users to use Payment Element instead of the Stripe Elements described there (old line 22). Preserve this integration-path qualification when surfacing old instructions; the new index calls the path Advanced integration but supplies no implementation content.

Old capture distinguishes customer-configured Accounts v2 and Customers v1 (old lines 8-14, 48-99), server subscription creation versus client bank collection/mandate confirmation (old lines 42-102, 104-221), and sandbox examples versus live settlement (old lines 312-355 and 891-938). The index does not settle any of those boundaries.

The old hosted path says ACH is delayed notification: checkout.session.completed is debit authorization, while async_payment_succeeded or invoice.paid supports fulfillment (old lines 732-769). The new index does not itself prove authorization, payment success, funds availability or bank receipt.

A separate existing knowledge conflict remains even though the November URL is navigation-only: wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:20 categorically says async methods including ACH skip incomplete and go directly active. The May web Elements guide instead instructs creating this subscription with payment_behavior=default_incomplete and status incomplete (old line 46), then says the microdeposit branch remains incomplete until verification while instant verification becomes active (old lines 221-225). The source's Elements setup at lines 22-43 is consistent with that dated guide. A reciprocal concept qualification should distinguish this Elements microdeposit path; the November index cannot establish current variant status rules.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep existing source statements about the Elements route, microdeposit extension and limits, default payment method webhook, trial SetupIntent, and Checkout webhook/fulfillment sequence attributed to the May 2026 full guide (source lines 11-70; old lines 42-470 and 671-769).

Keep the 10-day verification window qualified as microdeposit verification for a subscription and capped by the billing cycle date (old line 225), rather than a universal ACH payment or settlement deadline.

Keep the old guide's Accounts v2 availability and preview-version scope (old lines 8-14), and its Payment Element recommendation for new users on the advanced route (old line 22), as May snapshot claims.
Keep sandbox test account, email and instant-settlement statements distinct from live payment outcomes (old lines 312-355 and 891-938).
conflicts: wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:20 says ACH and other asynchronous methods skip incomplete and go straight to active. That categorical statement conflicts with the dated May ACH Elements guide: old raw line 46 creates an incomplete subscription using default_incomplete, and old lines 221-225 say it remains incomplete during microdeposit verification, versus active after instant verification. Qualify the concept reciprocally with this path and date, linking [[source-stripe-subscriptions-ach-debit]], without treating new index lines 9-14 as current behavioral confirmation.
unresolved_questions: What do the two November web variant pages actually say about current Elements and hosted Checkout flows? The new canonical index gives only their URLs; neither was captured or read in this assignment.
Do old parameter shapes, default payment method setup, microdeposit window, payment state and webhook timing still apply to each variant as of November 2026? The index cannot establish this.

Does any account currently qualify for Accounts v2 preview, and did any ACH debit actually settle? Neither the new index nor the historical guide establishes account-specific eligibility or a live outcome.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/ach-debit, the November capture establishes only that the ACH subscription article now routes readers to web Advanced integration and Full hosted page variants (new lines 5-14). It does not restate prerequisites, customer identities, PaymentIntent or SetupIntent states, verification limits, or payment finality. The May capture separately documents Elements and hosted routes, Accounts v2 versus Customers v1, microdeposit verification and delayed Checkout payment notifications (old lines 8-22, 221-249, 500-504, 732-769). [[source-stripe-subscriptions-ach-debit]] summarizes that May guide and remains dated to it (source lines 4-7).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/ach-debit, the November capture is a navigation split to Elements and Stripe-hosted variants (new lines 9-14), while the May capture contained both full sections (old lines 18-20 and 500-504); it establishes no substantive change or deprecation. [[source-stripe-subscriptions-ach-debit]] retains dated evidence for the microdeposit window, default payment method webhook, trial SetupIntent and delayed fulfillment (source lines 41-70; old lines 225, 273-300, 405-470, 732-769). A reciprocal warning is needed for wiki/concepts/stripe-subscriptions.md:20: its categorical ACH-skips-incomplete claim conflicts with the May Elements default_incomplete creation and incomplete microdeposit state (old lines 46 and 221-225). The index has no state detail to settle current behavior, account eligibility, payment success or bank receipt.
